name: Smile from the Streets You Hold

podcast.body: Recorded during Frusciante's deepest period of drug abuse, this album is considered one of his most heartbreaking works. Although the lyrics might not explicitly convey extreme sadness, the manner of playing and singing reveals the state of a man "almost dead, abandoned to his fate, without energy." The material for this album largely consisted of old recordings from his time with Red Hot Chili Peppers, repurposed and recorded in his dire condition. "la grabación de ese disco de John Frostyante es la grabación de un hombre que está casi muerto que está casi abandonado su suerte que está sin energia."

srcs.episode: La historia de John Frusciante: Talento, creatividad y guitarras.

podcast.body: Released in 1997, John Frusciante admitted to creating this record specifically to make drug money. During its recording, he claimed to be in verbal communication with spirits who gave him ideas for the music, stating his concern for his fame in their world over his fame in this one. The late River Phoenix appears on the song "Higher Down," and the track "For Air" features Frusciante taking a hit from a bong. "I was having verbal communications with the spirits while I was recording."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was released by John Frusciante during a period of deep heroin addiction. Its opening track, "Enter a Uh," is an 8-minute piece described as "not normal" due to its disturbing vocalizations. Frusciante later admitted the album was primarily intended to raise drug money and has since had it withdrawn from sale, though its presence on the internet persists. "In 1997, he released an album entitled Smile from the Streets You Hold and the opening track is called Enter a Ah."
